title: Raise connection pool limits
summary: A performance fix raises pool and worker limits after a checkout slowdown. Decide whether the change is safe for the shared database.
context: This change responds to checkout latency spikes during a sale by raising connection pool limits and the worker count. The service runs under Gunicorn with synchronous workers and shares a PostgreSQL 16 database, configured with max_connections = 100, with a background job worker.

provenance.notes: Draft written to prove the review contract. It introduces the pool setting used in the connection-exhaustion Challenge.

findings.title: Pool limits exceed the database connection budget
findings.explanation: Each Gunicorn worker process has its own pool. With 8 workers, pool_size=20 and max_overflow=20 allow up to 320 connections, while PostgreSQL accepts 100 and the job worker shares that limit. Under load the database refuses new connections, including the job worker's.

findings.title: A 60-second pool timeout hides exhaustion
findings.explanation: Requests wait up to 60 seconds for a free connection, longer than the 30-second Gunicorn worker timeout. Workers are killed mid-request instead of failing fast with a clear pool error, which makes exhaustion harder to diagnose.

findings.title: Doubling workers doubles connection demand
findings.explanation: Worker count multiplies every per-process pool. Raising it without reducing pool size or measuring the database budget turns a latency problem into a connection outage.
